text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Association of General Retailers and Traders insists government should pay for cash register modifications to meet new tax system replacing VAT on July 1. Modifications are needed because tax will now be charged at five percent, instead of 15 percent, and fiscal receipts will serve as tickets for a government-run lottery being held fortnightly. Government says retailers should pay for the modifications because advantages have been given to them in other areas with introduction of the tax.
- New Palestinian ambassador presents his credentials. Palestinian embassy might be reopened after having been closed for the past two years for financial reasons.

- General Workers' Union general secretary Jack Calamatta addresses International Labour Organization conference. Tells conference that definite contracts of work should not be continually renewed but should become indefinite after being renewed for more than one year.

- Air Malta offers free trip for passengers on hijacked aircraft. Eighty passengers and crew on board a flight to Istanbul hijacked to Cologne on Monday have been offered a free return trip to any destination serviced by the airline. No one was injured in the hijack, the first in Air Malta's history.
